title: Indian cardinal opposes ban on Latin Mass if Vatican II is not rejected
description: Bringing you the news from a traditional Catholic perspective. ( LifeSiteNews ) – Cardinal Oswald Gracias, the archbishop emeritus of Bombay, said during an interview that he is opposed to restrictions on the celebration of the Traditional Latin Mass (TLM) as long as its celebration does not indicate a “rejection” of the Second Vatican Council among the faithful. … The Vatican Secretariat of State had also denied permission for Bishop Schneider to celebrate the pilgrimage’s Pontifical Mass in the Basilica despite seeking Pope Leo’s explicit permission months in advance. CONFIRMED: TLM pilgrimage sought permission from Leo XIV months in advance “The Secretariat of State sent the organizers a letter explaining that, at least for this year, permission for the Pontifical Mass in St. Peter’s Basilica will not be granted,” a source very close to the traditional pilgrimage’s organizers previously told LifeSite. “The real reasons are unknown. It seems very strange that today the so-called LGBT Catholics can obtain a special Mass in St. Peter’s more easily than Catholics attached to the Church’s Tradition.”

title: Opposing Communion in the hand ‘extremist’? Church history disagrees
description: The Vatican’s Dicastery for Divine Worship warned against “liturgical extremism,” targeting Catholics who raise questions about kneeling for Communion, receiving on the tongue, and women’s chapel veils. Church historian Dr. Ed Mazza joins John-Henry Westen to contrast the Vatican’s position with statements from Cardinal Robert Sarah, Bishop Athanasius Schneider, and accounts attributed to Mother Teresa. Receiving Communion kneeling and on the tongue, Mazza argues, better expresses reverence for The expansion of Communion in the hand during the late 1960s and 1970s includes allegations concerning Cardinal Joseph Bernardin’s role in securing its approval by the American bishops in 1977. title: Pastor sentenced to probation after retrial over drag queen event protest
description: CALGARY, Alberta ( LifeSiteNews ) — Canadian pastor Derek Reimer was sentenced to 12 months of probation after a retrial stemming from an appeal after being found guilty of mischief and causing a disturbance for protesting a “drag queen story hour” event marketed to children at a public library, after a retrial 0that came from an appeal. Reimer learned of the sentencing by a Calgary judge on November 2, meaning he will now be under strict limitations on moving about freely. He is also banned from using social media, but it is up to his probation officer to enforce the ban. … However, the Crown appealed the ruling with a surprise visit to his house later in the year, claiming that Judge Allan Fradsham’s 2024 acquittal was incorrect. Court of King’s Bench Justice Nancy Carruthers allowed the appeal to move forward, stating that legal errors were made in the acquittal that led to the recent verdict. In 2025, Reimer was released from jail after earlier in the month being arrested for refusing to comply with a court order mandating he write a formal apology to the Calgary Public Library manager after criticizing him for promoting the “drag queen story hour” for children. Reimer has been in trouble many times for speaking out against the LGBT agenda targeting kids in public spaces.
